## Setup & Imports

### A test repository

The examples on this page run inside `GheasyTestRepo`, a throwaway Git
repository whose `origin` remote is a local bare repository. Both are
deleted when the `with` block ends.

``` python
import tempfile, shutil
class GheasyTestRepo:
    'Context manager: real temp git repo with initialized git and fake remote.'
    def __enter__(self):
        self._tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        self.path = Path(self._tmp)
        # bare repo to push to
        self._bare = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        sp.run(['git', 'init', '--bare', self._bare], check=True, capture_output=True)
        self.remote = f'file://{self._bare}'
        sp.run(['git', 'init', str(self.path)], check=True, capture_output=True)
        sp.run(['git', '-C', str(self.path), 'remote', 'add', 'origin', self.remote], check=True, capture_output=True)
        sp.run(['git', '-C', str(self.path), 'config', 'user.email', 'test@test.com'], check=True, capture_output=True)
        sp.run(['git', '-C', str(self.path), 'config', 'user.name', 'Test'], check=True, capture_output=True)
        return self
    def __exit__(self, *a):
        shutil.rmtree(self._tmp, ignore_errors=True)
        shutil.rmtree(self._bare, ignore_errors=True)
```

``` python
with GheasyTestRepo() as t:
    assert t.path.exists()
    assert (t.path / '.git').is_dir()
    assert t.remote.startswith('file://')
    print('GheasyTestRepo OK')
```

    GheasyTestRepo OK

## Config

[`GheasyConfig`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gheasyconfig)
is the contents of `.gheasy/config.json` as a Python object. Its app
field holds the project name. `envs` holds one
[`EnvConfig`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#envconfig)
per place the app is deployed, such as `prod` or `staging`; each records
the server’s host, the domain it serves, the branch that deploys there,
and the app’s folder on the server. The remaining fields feed the
generators further down. `workflows` and `workflow_preset` choose the CI
jobs, `test_cmd` replaces pytest, `deploy_cmd` is the shell command a
deploy job runs, `extra_jobs` holds custom jobs, `env_schema` decides
which settings become secrets, and `hooks` and `lfs` set up the local
repository.

`add_env`, `set_lfs`, `set_hooks`, `set_workflows` and `add_job` change
the config and return it, so calls can be chained before `save`. `load`
reads the file, and returns an empty config when there is none.
`from_pyproject` starts a config named after the project in
`pyproject.toml`.

## Generators

The `mk_*` functions turn a config into the contents of a file and
return it as text; the `gh_*` functions further down write the files.

[`mk_deploy_job`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#mk_deploy_job)
adds one environment’s deploy job to a
[`Workflow`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/workflow.html#workflow)
builder. The job waits for `test`, runs only for pushes to that
environment’s branch, writes the `DEPLOY_KEY` secret out as an SSH key,
adds the server to `known_hosts`, and then runs the deploy command. The
command is the `cmd` you pass, or the config’s `deploy_cmd`; with
neither, it prints a warning and adds nothing.

<a

### mk_deploy_job

``` python
def mk_deploy_job(
    env_name, cfg, wfb, cmd:NoneType=None
):
```

*Add the deploy job for `env_name` to the workflow builder `wfb`, or
warn and add nothing when there is no deploy command.*

``` python
from fastcore.all import AttrDict
from fastcore.test import test_eq
test_eq(_res_wfs(AttrDict(workflows=['test', 'lint'], workflow_preset=None)), {'test': True, 'lint': True})   # gh_init stores gh_new's list
test_eq(_res_wfs(AttrDict(workflows={'test': False}, workflow_preset='rust')), {'rust': True, 'test': False})
```

``` python
from fastcore.test import test_eq

# No deploy cmd → None returned, job not added to wfb
cfg_no_cmd = GheasyConfig(app='myapp')
cfg_no_cmd.add_env('prod', '1.2.3.4', 'myapp.com')
wfb_no = Workflow('test')
wfb_no.on.push()
result = mk_deploy_job('prod', cfg_no_cmd, wfb_no)
assert result is None
assert 'deploy-prod' not in wfb_no._job_map

# cmd= takes priority over cfg.deploy_cmd
cfg_cmd = GheasyConfig(app='myapp', deploy_cmd='cfg_deploy.sh')
cfg_cmd.add_env('prod', '1.2.3.4', 'myapp.com')
wfb_cmd = Workflow('test')
mk_deploy_job('prod', cfg_cmd, wfb_cmd, cmd='override.sh')
jb = wfb_cmd._job_map['deploy-prod']
deploy_step = next(s for s in jb._steps if s._data.get('name') == 'Deploy to prod')
test_eq(deploy_step._data['run'], 'override.sh')

# cfg.deploy_cmd used when cmd not passed
wfb2 = Workflow('test')
mk_deploy_job('prod', cfg_cmd, wfb2)
jb2 = wfb2._job_map['deploy-prod']
deploy_step2 = next(s for s in jb2._steps if s._data.get('name') == 'Deploy to prod')
test_eq(deploy_step2._data['run'], 'cfg_deploy.sh')

# SSH key step always present
ssh = next(s for s in jb2._steps if s._data.get('name') == 'Deploy SSH key')
assert 'id_rsa' in ssh._data['run']

# Job has correct runner, needs, environment, branch gate
test_eq(jb2._data['runs-on'], 'ubuntu-latest')
test_eq(jb2._data['needs'], 'test')
test_eq(jb2._data['environment'], 'prod')
test_eq(jb2._data['if'], "github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'")

# uv shortcuts used: setup-uv step present (no manual uses/step call)
setup_uv_step = next(s for s in jb2._steps if s._data.get('uses') == 'astral-sh/setup-uv@v5')
assert setup_uv_step is not None

print('mk_deploy_job OK')
```

## Workflow generation

[`mk_workflow`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#mk_workflow)
builds the whole CI workflow for a config and returns it as YAML text,
headed by a comment saying gheasy manages the file. Which jobs it
includes is decided in three layers, each overriding the one before: the
preset named in `workflow_preset`, the flags in `cfg.workflows`, and the
keyword arguments you pass. A preset only switches on a language job:
`rust` and `go` turn on the job of the same name, `fastapi-react` and
`nodejs` turn on `node`, and `python` and `fasthtml` turn on nothing.

The `publish` and `docker` jobs wait for `test`, so keep `test` on when
you use them. The workflow runs on pushes to the branches named in
`cfg.envs`, or to main when there are no environments. Each environment
gets a deploy job from
[`mk_deploy_job`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#mk_deploy_job),
and the custom jobs in `cfg.extra_jobs` are added last.
[`gh_workflow`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_workflow)
writes the result to `.github/workflows/gheasy.yml`. Regenerate that
file rather than editing it, because the next regeneration overwrites
hand edits.

### mk_workflow

``` python
def mk_workflow(
    cfg, *, on_pull_request:bool | None=None, # also run on pull requests, not only pushes
    test:bool | None=None, # uv test job: `uv run pytest`, or cfg.test_cmd
    lint:bool | None=None, # ruff check and format check
    publish_pypi:bool | None=None, # PyPI trusted publishing on release events, after test
    docker_build:bool | None=None, # Docker build and push to GHCR, after test
    node:bool | None=None, # `frontend` job: npm ci, build and test
    rust:bool | None=None, # Rust build, test and clippy
    go:bool | None=None, # Go build, test and vet
):
```

*Build the CI workflow YAML for `cfg`; a flag left as `None` takes its
value from the config’s preset and `workflows`.*

``` python
# deploy skipped when no deploy_cmd
cfg_no_deploy = GheasyConfig(app='myapp')
cfg_no_deploy.add_env('prod', '1.2.3.4', 'myapp.com')
wf_str = mk_workflow(cfg_no_deploy)
assert 'deploy-prod' not in wf_str
assert '# Managed by gheasy' in wf_str

# deploy included when deploy_cmd set
cfg = GheasyConfig(app='myapp', deploy_cmd='./deploy.sh')
cfg.add_env('prod', '1.2.3.4', 'myapp.com')
wf_str2 = mk_workflow(cfg)
assert 'deploy-prod' in wf_str2

# explicit flag=True overrides cfg (no flags in cfg, test=True via kwarg)
wf_test = mk_workflow(cfg, test=True)
assert 'uv run pytest' in wf_test
assert 'jobs:\n  test:' in wf_test or 'test:' in wf_test

# explicit flag=False suppresses even if cfg would enable it
cfg_with_test = GheasyConfig(app='myapp', workflows={'test': True})
cfg_with_test.add_env('prod', '1.2.3.4', 'myapp.com')
cfg_with_test.deploy_cmd = './deploy.sh'
wf_notests = mk_workflow(cfg_with_test, test=False)
assert 'uv run pytest' not in wf_notests

# lint + test via kwargs
wf_lint = mk_workflow(cfg, test=True, lint=True)
assert 'ruff' in wf_lint
assert 'needs: test' in wf_lint or 'needs: test' in wf_lint.replace("'", "")

# on_pull_request adds pull_request trigger
wf_pr = mk_workflow(cfg, on_pull_request=True)
assert 'pull_request:' in wf_pr

# workflow_preset='rust' enables rust job by default
cfg_rust = GheasyConfig(app='myrust', workflow_preset='rust')
wf_rust = mk_workflow(cfg_rust)
assert 'dtolnay/rust-toolchain' in wf_rust

print('mk_workflow OK')
```

## .gitattributes generation

`.gitattributes` tells Git how to treat files that match a pattern, and
Git LFS needs one line there for every pattern it handles.
[`mk_gitattributes`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#mk_gitattributes)
writes those lines between `# BEGIN gheasy-lfs` and `# END gheasy-lfs`
markers, so that
[`gh_gitattributes`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_gitattributes)
can later replace just that block and keep any lines you added yourself.
[`mk_hook`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#mk_hook)
wraps a command in a bash script between similar markers,
`# BEGIN gheasy-managed` and `# END gheasy-managed`, for
[`gh_hooks`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_hooks) to
install.

[`mk_dependabot`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#mk_dependabot)
writes a `.github/dependabot.yml`, the file that asks GitHub’s
Dependabot to open pull requests when your dependencies have new
versions. By default it checks pip packages and GitHub Actions every
week.

``` python
# mk_gitattributes
out = mk_gitattributes(['*.pt', '*.onnx'])
assert '# BEGIN gheasy-lfs' in out
assert '# END gheasy-lfs' in out
assert '*.pt filter=lfs diff=lfs merge=lfs -text' in out

# mk_hook
h = mk_hook('uv run nbdev_prepare')
assert '#!/bin/bash' in h
assert 'gheasy-managed' in h
assert 'uv run nbdev_prepare' in h

# mk_workflow — no lint by default
cfg = GheasyConfig(app='myapp', workflow_preset='python')
cfg.add_env('prod', '1.2.3.4', 'myapp.com')
wf = mk_workflow(cfg)
assert '# Managed by gheasy' in wf
assert 'myapp CI' in wf
assert 'lint' not in wf

# mk_workflow — lint opt-in
cfg2 = GheasyConfig(app='myapp', workflow_preset='python', workflows={'lint': True})
cfg2.add_env('prod', '1.2.3.4', 'myapp.com')
assert 'lint' in mk_workflow(cfg2)

# preset override — disable test
cfg3 = GheasyConfig(app='myapp', workflow_preset='fasthtml', workflows={'test': False})
cfg3.add_env('prod', '1.2.3.4', 'myapp.com')
assert 'test:' not in mk_workflow(cfg3)
print('generators OK')
```

## Local Git setup

The next functions change files inside your checkout: hook scripts in
`.git/hooks/` and the LFS block in `.gitattributes`.

## Git hooks

A git hook is a script Git runs at a fixed moment, such as `pre-commit`,
which runs just before each commit and can stop it.
[`gh_hooks`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_hooks)
installs hooks from a dict of hook name to command, where a command is a
string or a list of lines. Without a dict it uses `hooks` from the
config. It writes each script into `.git/hooks/` between gheasy’s
markers and makes it executable. Running it again replaces only the
marked block, so anything you wrote above or below it stays.

[`nbdev_hook`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#nbdev_hook)
returns the usual command for an nbdev project,
`uv run --with nbdev nbdev-prepare`, which exports, tests and cleans the
notebooks before every commit.
[`gh_githooks_pre_commit`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_githooks_pre_commit)
installs that command, or the one you pass, as the `pre-commit` hook.

Git never commits the contents of `.git/hooks/`, so these hooks stay on
your machine and each new clone needs them installed once.
[`gh_setup`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_setup)
and
[`GheasyRepo.new`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gheasyrepo.new)
do that for you. When hooks have to be shared across many repositories,
or are written in several languages, the `pre-commit` package is the
better tool.

### nbdev_hook

``` python
def nbdev_hook():
```

*Return the pre-commit command that runs `nbdev-prepare` through uv,
adding nbdev even when the project does not depend on it.*

``` python
import tempfile, shutil
```

``` python
# No .git dir → warns and returns (no error)
tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
try: gh_hooks({'pre-commit': 'echo hi'}, path=tmp)  # should print warning, not raise
finally: shutil.rmtree(tmp)

# Missing hooks/ subdir → created automatically (rmtree to clear git init's sample files)
with GheasyTestRepo() as t:
    shutil.rmtree(t.path / '.git' / 'hooks')
    gh_hooks({'pre-commit': 'echo hi'}, path=t.path)
    assert (t.path / '.git' / 'hooks' / 'pre-commit').exists()

# No arg → reads from cfg.hooks
with GheasyTestRepo() as t:
    GheasyConfig(app='myapp', hooks={'pre-commit': 'echo test'}).save(t.path)
    gh_hooks(path=t.path)
    content = (t.path / '.git' / 'hooks' / 'pre-commit').read_text()
    assert 'echo test' in content

# No arg, no config → warns and returns (no error)
with GheasyTestRepo() as t: gh_hooks(path=t.path)

# list[str] cmd → joined with newlines, all commands present in hook
with GheasyTestRepo() as t:
    gh_hooks({'pre-commit': ['uv run ruff check .', 'uv run nbdev-prepare']}, path=t.path)
    content = (t.path / '.git' / 'hooks' / 'pre-commit').read_text()
    assert 'uv run ruff check .' in content
    assert 'uv run nbdev-prepare' in content

# nbdev_hook() returns the --with nbdev form (hyphenated nbdev-prepare)
assert 'nbdev-prepare' in nbdev_hook()
assert '--with nbdev' in nbdev_hook()

# gh_githooks_pre_commit defaults to nbdev_hook()
with GheasyTestRepo() as t:
    gh_githooks_pre_commit(path=t.path)
    content = (t.path / '.git' / 'hooks' / 'pre-commit').read_text()
    assert '--with nbdev' in content

print('gh_hooks OK')
```

## LFS and .gitattributes

Large binary files such as model weights and databases make a repository
slow to clone, because every version stays in the history. Git LFS
stores them on a separate server and commits a small pointer file in
their place.
[`gh_lfs`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_lfs) runs
`git lfs install`, then `git lfs track` for each pattern, and saves the
patterns to the config. Without patterns it tracks a default list:
`*.db`, `*.onnx`, `*.bin`, `*.pt`, `*.pkl`, `*.safetensors`, `*.tar.gz`,
`*.mp4` and `*.parquet`.

[`gh_gitattributes`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_gitattributes)
rewrites the gheasy block in `.gitattributes` from the patterns in the
config and leaves every other line alone, so attributes you added
yourself, such as `*.sh text eol=lf`, survive. Run it after changing the
patterns in the config.

``` python
gh_lfs(['*.onnx', '*.db', '*.safetensors'])  # once per repository
gh_gitattributes()                           # after any change to the patterns in the config
# then: git add .gitattributes && git commit -m 'chore: update .gitattributes'
```

``` python
# gh_hooks installs hook and makes it executable
with GheasyTestRepo() as t:
    gh_hooks({'pre-commit': 'uv run nbdev_prepare'}, path=t.path)
    hook_path = t.path / '.git' / 'hooks' / 'pre-commit'
    assert hook_path.exists()
    text = hook_path.read_text()
    assert '# BEGIN gheasy-managed' in text
    assert 'uv run nbdev_prepare' in text
    assert hook_path.stat().st_mode & stat.S_IXUSR

# re-running updates only managed block, preserves user content
with GheasyTestRepo() as t:
    (t.path / '.git' / 'hooks' / 'pre-commit').write_text('# user content\n')
    gh_hooks({'pre-commit': 'uv run nbdev_prepare'}, path=t.path)
    text = (t.path / '.git' / 'hooks' / 'pre-commit').read_text()
    assert '# user content' in text
    assert 'uv run nbdev_prepare' in text
    gh_hooks({'pre-commit': 'uv run pytest'}, path=t.path)
    text2 = (t.path / '.git' / 'hooks' / 'pre-commit').read_text()
    assert 'uv run pytest' in text2
    assert text2.count('BEGIN gheasy-managed') == 1

# gh_gitattributes writes and updates managed block
with GheasyTestRepo() as t:
    GheasyConfig(app='test').set_lfs(['*.pt', '*.onnx']).save(t.path)
    gh_gitattributes(path=t.path)
    ga = (t.path / '.gitattributes').read_text()
    assert '# BEGIN gheasy-lfs' in ga
    assert '*.pt filter=lfs' in ga

print('git ops OK')
```

## GitHub settings

The functions from here on change settings stored on GitHub, not files
in your checkout.

## Finding the repository and the token

[`gh_api`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_api) works
out which GitHub repository a checkout belongs to from the URL of its
`origin` remote, and returns the owner, the repository name and a ghapi
client bound to it. It raises `ValueError` when the remote is missing or
does not look like `owner/repo`.
[`gh_token`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_token)
returns the token you pass, or the `GITHUB_TOKEN` environment variable
when you pass nothing.

## Repository settings

Branch protection is a set of rules GitHub enforces on a branch, such as
requiring an approving review or passing checks before a pull request
can merge.
[`gh_protect`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_protect)
sets those rules for one branch: how many approvals are needed, whether
a new push dismisses earlier approvals, which status checks must pass,
whether administrators are bound by the rules too, and whether force
pushes are allowed.
[`gh_topics`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_topics)
replaces the repository’s topics, the tags shown on its GitHub page, and
lowercases each one because GitHub requires it. Both need a token whose
owner is an administrator of the repository.

``` python
gh_protect('main',
    require_reviews=1,
    require_status_checks=['test', 'lint'],
    dismiss_stale=True)
```

## Secrets and variables

GitHub Actions jobs read their settings from two stores. A secret is
encrypted and hidden in logs; a variable is plain text.
[`gh_secret`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_secret)
sets one secret with `gh secret set`. With `env='prod'` it scopes the
secret to the GitHub environment `prod`, so only jobs that deploy there
can read it.
[`gh_secrets_from_file`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_secrets_from_file)
sets every `KEY=VALUE` line of a file such as `.env` as a secret. Use
[`gh_push_env`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_push_env)
when some values should be variables: it takes a dict and uses the
config’s `env_schema` to choose, sending a key whose schema default is
`None` to the secrets and a key with a string default to the variables.
All three accept `dry_run=True`, which prints the `gh` commands instead
of running them.

[`gh_deploy_key_setup`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_deploy_key_setup)
uploads an SSH private key as the `DEPLOY_KEY` secret that the deploy
jobs from
[`mk_deploy_job`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#mk_deploy_job)
use to reach the server. Two steps come first and are yours to do:
create the key pair with `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f deploy_key`, and add
the public key to the server’s `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`.

These functions need the `gh` command line tool installed and logged in
(`gh auth login`).

``` python
import io, contextlib

# gh_push_env dry-run routes correctly
with GheasyTestRepo() as t:
    cfg = GheasyConfig(app='test', env_schema={'DB_URL': None, 'APP_ENV': 'dev'})
    cfg.save(t.path)
    buf = io.StringIO()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf):
        gh_push_env({'DB_URL': 'postgres://...', 'APP_ENV': 'prod'}, dry_run=True, path=t.path)
    out = buf.getvalue()
    assert 'secret set DB_URL' in out
    assert 'variable set APP_ENV' in out

print('github ops OK')
```

## Lifecycle

## Naming a repository

Functions that take a GitHub repository accept it in three forms: an
`owner/repo` string, a GitHub URL such as
`https://github.com/owner/repo`, or a local path whose `origin` remote
points at GitHub.
[`_resolve_gh_repo_input`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#_resolve_gh_repo_input)
turns any of them into an `(owner, repo)` pair, and
[`_git_branch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#_git_branch)
reads the branch a checkout is on, falling back to main.

## The pull request a branch belongs to

An editor’s status line wants to say whether the current branch has an
open pull request on GitHub and how it stands.
`pr_context(path, branch)` answers that. It returns the pull request’s
number, title and link, the branch it targets (its base), whether it is
a draft, GitHub’s merge state, how many commits the branch is ahead of
the base and how many the base has gained since the branch split off,
and the total, failing and pending checks on the branch’s latest commit.
The answer is cached for a minute, because a status line asks far more
often than a pull request changes.

[`pr_context`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#pr_context)
never raises. When there is no open pull request, no GitHub remote, no
token, or GitHub refuses the request, `pr` is `None` and `note` says
why. The example below runs
[`_checks`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#_checks), the
part that counts checks, against a fake API.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/core.py#L352"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### pr_context

``` python
def pr_context(
    path, branch
):
```

*Return the open pull request for `branch`, how far its base has moved,
and its checks, or `pr=None` with the reason in `note`.*

``` python
class _FakeChecks:
    def __init__(self, runs): self.runs = runs
    def list_for_ref(self, sha, per_page): return {'check_runs': self.runs}
class _FakeApi:
    def __init__(self, runs): self.checks = _FakeChecks(runs)

api = _FakeApi([{'name': 'test', 'status': 'completed', 'conclusion': 'success'},
                {'name': 'lint', 'status': 'completed', 'conclusion': 'failure'},
                {'name': 'docs', 'status': 'in_progress', 'conclusion': None},
                {'name': 'old', 'status': 'completed', 'conclusion': 'skipped'}])
_checks(api, 'abc1234')
```

A repository with no GitHub remote gets the same answer as every other
failure: `pr` is `None` and `note` explains.

``` python
bare = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
sp.run(['git', 'init', str(bare)], check=True, capture_output=True)
ctx = pr_context(str(bare), 'main')
test_eq(ctx['pr'], None)
assert 'no GitHub remote' in ctx['note']
test_fail(lambda: _pr_api(str(bare)), contains='no GitHub remote')
shutil.rmtree(bare, ignore_errors=True)
ctx['note']
```

## Setting up a project

These are the main entry points, and all but
[`gh_record_deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_record_deploy)
are also `gheasy` commands. They read and write `.gheasy/config.json`
and print what to do next.

[`gh_init`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_init)
writes a new config with one environment, replacing any config already
there; without `branch` it uses the branch you have checked out.
[`gh_add_env`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_add_env)
adds or replaces an environment and rewrites
`.github/workflows/gheasy.yml` at once.
[`gh_add_job`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_add_job)
stores a custom job, written as the dict you would put under `jobs:` in
the YAML, for the next workflow build.
[`gh_workflow`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_workflow)
writes the workflow file, and with a token it also commits the file to
GitHub through the API.
[`gh_status`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_status)
prints a table of the deploys recorded so far, and
[`gh_ship`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_ship) runs
[`gh_workflow`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_workflow)
and then
[`gh_status`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_status).
[`gh_record_deploy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_record_deploy)
is the call a deploy job makes at the end to record which commit it
shipped and when.

``` python
with GheasyTestRepo() as t:
    gh_init('myapp', '1.2.3.4', 'myapp.com', path=t.path)
    assert cfg_path(t.path).exists()
    cfg = GheasyConfig.load(t.path)
    assert cfg.app == 'myapp'
    assert 'prod' in cfg.envs

with GheasyTestRepo() as t:
    gh_init('myapp', '1.2.3.4', 'myapp.com', path=t.path)
    gh_add_env('staging', '5.6.7.8', 'staging.myapp.com', path=t.path)
    cfg = GheasyConfig.load(t.path)
    assert 'staging' in cfg.envs
    wf_path = t.path / '.github' / 'workflows' / 'gheasy.yml'
    assert wf_path.exists()
    # no deploy_cmd set → workflow exists but no deploy job
    assert '# Managed by gheasy' in wf_path.read_text()

with GheasyTestRepo() as t:
    # with deploy_cmd → deploy job included in workflow
    gh_init('myapp', '1.2.3.4', 'myapp.com', path=t.path, deploy_cmd='./deploy.sh')
    gh_add_env('staging', '5.6.7.8', 'staging.myapp.com', path=t.path)
    wf_path = t.path / '.github' / 'workflows' / 'gheasy.yml'
    assert 'deploy-staging' in wf_path.read_text()

with GheasyTestRepo() as t:
    gh_init('myapp', '1.2.3.4', 'myapp.com', path=t.path)
    gh_workflow(path=t.path)
    wf_path = t.path / '.github' / 'workflows' / 'gheasy.yml'
    assert '# Managed by gheasy' in wf_path.read_text()

print('lifecycle OK')
```

## One-call setup

[`gh_setup`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_setup) is
what you run once in a new project. It calls
[`gh_init`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_init),
writes the workflow with
[`gh_workflow`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_workflow),
and installs a pre-commit hook that runs `uv run nbdev_prepare`. Pass a
`hooks` dict to install other hooks instead, or `hooks={}` to install
none. After that,
[`gh_add_env`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_add_env)
and [`gh_ship`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_ship)
cover most changes.

``` python
gh_setup('myapp', '1.2.3.4', 'myapp.example.com',
         env_schema={'DB_URL': None, 'PORT': '8000'},
         workflows={'lint': True})
# writes .gheasy/config.json
# writes .github/workflows/gheasy.yml
# installs a pre-commit hook that runs: uv run nbdev_prepare
```

Later, to add a staging server that deploys from `dev`:

``` python
gh_add_env('staging', '5.6.7.8', 'staging.myapp.com', branch='dev')
gh_ship()  # rewrite the workflow and print the deploy table
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/core.py#L456"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### gh_setup

``` python
def gh_setup(
    name, host, domain, env:str='prod', branch:NoneType=None, srv_path:str='/srv/app', test_cmd:NoneType=None,
    env_schema:NoneType=None, token:NoneType=None, hooks:NoneType=None, hook_cmd:str='uv run nbdev_prepare',
    lfs:NoneType=None, workflows:NoneType=None, workflow_preset:NoneType=None, deploy_cmd:NoneType=None,
    path:str='.'
):
```

*Set up a project in one call: write the config and the workflow, and
install hooks (`hooks={}` installs none).*

``` python
with GheasyTestRepo() as t:
    result = gh_setup('myapp', '1.2.3.4', 'myapp.com', path=t.path)
    assert result == cfg_path(t.path)
    assert cfg_path(t.path).exists()
    assert (t.path / '.github' / 'workflows' / 'gheasy.yml').exists()
    hook = (t.path / '.git' / 'hooks' / 'pre-commit').read_text()
    assert 'nbdev_prepare' in hook

with GheasyTestRepo() as t:
    gh_setup('myapp', '1.2.3.4', 'myapp.com', hooks={}, path=t.path)
    assert not (t.path / '.git' / 'hooks' / 'pre-commit').exists()

print('gh_setup OK')
```

## Repository health

[`gh_check`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_check)
audits a repository against gheasy’s defaults and returns a list of
findings. In the checkout it looks for gheasy’s pre-commit hook, for the
LFS block in `.gitattributes`, and for a `pyproject.toml` that builds
with hatchling. With a token it also asks GitHub whether the repository
has topics and a `.github/dependabot.yml`.
[`gh_apply`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_apply)
then runs the fix of every finding that has one. `dry_run=True` lists
the fixes without running them, and `confirm=True` asks before each. The
local findings come with fixes; the GitHub ones only suggest what to
run.

## RepoFinding

Each finding is a
[`RepoFinding`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#repofinding).
It has a level (`ok`, `warn` or `error`), a category such as `hooks` or
`lfs`, a message, an optional function that fixes the problem, the
command that fix stands for, and a link to documentation. Printing a
finding shows a tick, a warning sign or a cross, then the category, the
message and the suggested command. `apply` runs the fix, or prints the
suggested command when there is no fix.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/core.py#L481"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
):
```

*Audit a repository: hook, LFS block and build backend locally, and
topics and dependabot on GitHub.*

## GheasyRepo

[`GheasyRepo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gheasyrepo)
holds a repository reference, a token and a local path, and runs the
functions above with them. Creating one makes no API calls; it only
parses the reference, which can be `owner/repo`, a GitHub URL, or a
local path with a GitHub remote. `check` and `apply` are
[`gh_check`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_check)
and
[`gh_apply`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_apply)
for that repository. `create` makes the repository on GitHub, under an
organisation when the owner is not the signed-in user.

[`GheasyRepo.new`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gheasyrepo.new)
scaffolds a whole project in one call. It creates the GitHub repository,
clones it, pins the Python version with `uv python pin`, runs
`nbdev-new` when the template is `nbdev`, converts `pyproject.toml` to
hatchling, sets up LFS with the default patterns, installs the nbdev
pre-commit hook, writes a workflow when you pass `workflows`, commits,
pushes, and sets the topics. The `gheasy gh-new` command calls it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/core.py#L555"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GheasyRepo

``` python
def GheasyRepo(
    ref:str=None, token:str=None, path:str='.'
)->None:
```

*A GitHub repository and a local path, with methods that run the `gh_*`
functions on them.*

``` python
with GheasyTestRepo() as t:
    findings = gh_check(path=t.path, remote=False)
    levels = [f.level for f in findings]
    assert 'warn' in levels

    gh_githooks_pre_commit(path=t.path)
    findings2 = gh_check(path=t.path, remote=False, verbose=False)
    hook_findings = [f for f in findings2 if f.category == FINDING_HOOKS]
    assert hook_findings[0].level == 'ok'

with GheasyTestRepo() as t:
    GheasyConfig(app='test').set_lfs(['*.pt']).save(t.path)
    findings = gh_check(path=t.path, remote=False, verbose=False)
    warn_before = sum(1 for f in findings if f.level == 'warn')
    gh_apply(findings)
    findings2 = gh_check(path=t.path, remote=False, verbose=False)
    warn_after = sum(1 for f in findings2 if f.level == 'warn')
    assert warn_after < warn_before

print('repo health OK')
```

## Migration

## pyproject.toml migration

gheasy expects projects to build with hatchling.
[`gh_pyproject_to_hatchling`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_pyproject_to_hatchling)
rewrites `pyproject.toml` to do so. It sets `[build-system]` to
hatchling and `requires-python` to `>=3.11`, points the wheel and the
version number at the package folder named after the project, limits the
source distribution to that folder, `README.md` and `pyproject.toml`,
and removes any `[tool.setuptools]` section. It edits the file with
tomlkit, which keeps your comments and formatting, and a second run
changes nothing. `dry_run=True` only prints which file it would change.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/core.py#L643"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### gh_pyproject_to_hatchling

``` python
def gh_pyproject_to_hatchling(
    path:str='.', dry_run:bool=False
):
```

*Rewrite `pyproject.toml` to build with hatchling; running it again
changes nothing.*

``` python
with GheasyTestRepo() as t:
    (t.path / 'pyproject.toml').write_text('''
[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "myapp"
''')
    changed = _migrate_pyproject_to_hatchling(t.path)
    assert changed
    import tomlkit
    doc = tomlkit.parse((t.path / 'pyproject.toml').read_text())
    assert doc['project']['requires-python'] == '>=3.11'
    assert doc['build-system']['build-backend'] == 'hatchling.build'
    targets = doc['tool']['hatch']['build']['targets']
    assert targets['wheel']['packages'] == ['myapp']
    assert targets['sdist']['include'] == ['/myapp', '/README.md', '/pyproject.toml']
    assert doc['tool']['hatch']['version']['path'] == 'myapp/__init__.py'
    changed2 = _migrate_pyproject_to_hatchling(t.path)
    assert not changed2, 'should be idempotent'

print('migration OK')
```

    migration OK

## Skill installation

Coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex read instructions from
`SKILL.md` files in a repository.
[`mv_skill_md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#mv_skill_md)
copies the `SKILL.md` that ships with gheasy into
`.claude/skills/gheasy/` and `.agents/skills/gheasy/`, at the root of
the repository that contains `path`. It defaults to `dry_run=True`,
which only prints where the files would go.
[`repo_root`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#repo_root)
finds that root by walking up from `path` to the first folder holding a
`.git`.

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

## CLI

Installing gheasy adds a `gheasy` command. Its subcommands are the
functions above with hyphens in their names, such as `gheasy gh-setup`
and `gheasy gh-check`, and `gheasy --help` lists them all.
[`gh_new`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gh_new) exists
for the command line: it is
[`GheasyRepo.new`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#gheasyrepo.new)
with `workflows` taken as a list of flag names.

``` bash
gheasy gh-new myorg/myrepo --workflows test lint --topics python nbdev --python 3.13
```

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/core.py#L670"

``` python
# Full remote lifecycle — requires GITHUB_TOKEN with repo scope
# Run manually: GheasyRepo.new('your-org/gheasy-test-repo')
import os
if os.environ.get('GITHUB_TOKEN'):
    with GheasyTestRepo() as r:
        # Remote check on a known public repo
        repo = GheasyRepo('AnswerDotAI/fastcore', token=os.environ['GITHUB_TOKEN'])
        findings = repo.check(local=False)
        cats = {f.category for f in findings}
        assert FINDING_BRANCH_PROTECTION in cats
        print(f'Remote check: {len(findings)} findings on AnswerDotAI/fastcore')
else:
    print('Skipped: GITHUB_TOKEN not set')
```
